content.user_title: Analyze Research Data With Statistical Tests
content.value_statement: Choosing and reporting statistics correctly is difficult under research deadlines. This skill guides test selection, assumption checks, effect sizes, power analysis, Bayesian methods, and APA reporting.
actual_capabilities: Select suitable tests for group comparisons, relationships, regression, and categorical outcomes.
Check normality, variance homogeneity, linearity, outliers, and regression diagnostics.
Run and interpret t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, correlations, and regression models.
Calculate effect sizes, confidence intervals, and sample size requirements.
Explain Bayesian alternatives, Bayes factors, credible intervals, and convergence checks.
Draft APA-style result summaries with assumptions, test statistics, p-values, and effect sizes.
limitations: It does not replace expert statistical review for high-stakes research decisions.
It depends on accurate data descriptions, variable definitions, and study design details.
It provides guidance and examples, but users must run analyses in their own environment.
It does not validate ethical approvals, consent procedures, or publication requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan A Study Analysis
use_cases.description: Choose tests, define assumptions, estimate sample size, and plan effect size reporting before collecting data.

use_cases.title: Review Experimental Results
use_cases.description: Check assumptions, compare groups, interpret post-hoc tests, and identify transparent reporting language.

use_cases.title: Prepare Manuscript Statistics
use_cases.description: Convert statistical outputs into APA-style text with confidence intervals, diagnostics, and cautious interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Test
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [outcome type], [predictor or group structure], and [sample size]. Which statistical test should I use, and what assumptions should I check?

prompt_templates.title: Check Assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this study design and variable list. Create an assumption-checking plan, including plots, tests, and actions for violations.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Interpret these statistical results for a research audience. Include effect size, confidence interval, practical meaning, and limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Full Analysis Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full analysis plan for this study, including primary tests, corrections, power analysis, sensitivity checks, Bayesian alternatives, and APA reporting language.

output_examples.input: Two independent groups with continuous scores and possible unequal variance.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: inspect distributions, test variance homogeneity, use Welch t-test if variance differs, report mean difference, confidence interval, and Cohen's d.

output_examples.input: Three treatment conditions with a significant omnibus ANOVA.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: report the ANOVA result, partial eta-squared, planned or corrected post-hoc comparisons, group means, and assumption checks.

output_examples.input: Small sample research question with interest in evidence for the null hypothesis.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: consider a Bayesian model, define priors clearly, report posterior intervals, Bayes factors, convergence diagnostics, and sensitivity to priors.

best_practices: Define hypotheses, outcomes, predictors, and exclusion rules before choosing tests.
Check assumptions and diagnostics before interpreting p-values or model coefficients.
Report effect sizes, intervals, sample sizes, and non-significant planned analyses.
anti_patterns: Do not test many alternatives until one result becomes significant.
Do not omit assumption violations or unexplained data exclusions.
Do not describe non-significant results as proof that no effect exists.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the correct statistical test?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses outcome type, group structure, sample size, and assumptions to recommend suitable tests and alternatives.

faq.question: Does it run analysis automatically?
faq.answer: It provides Python examples and a helper script for assumption checks, but users run analyses in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help with APA reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives templates for t-tests, ANOVA, regression, Bayesian results, assumptions, and null findings.

faq.question: Does it support Bayesian statistics?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains priors, Bayes factors, credible intervals, posterior checks, and common Bayesian models.

faq.question: Can it calculate power and sample size?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for a priori power, sensitivity analysis, and common effect size inputs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for high-stakes decisions?
faq.answer: Use it as guidance only. High-stakes medical, legal, or policy research needs review by a qualified statistician.
